scope: First seed-42 overlapping Wan expansion from the accepted frames 110-198 anchor toward the full 660-frame flower-arranging film
summary: All nine non-anchor raw windows were preserved, but dense review found source-human face or body regeneration in six difficult starts, so the batch is not stitchable and remains a negative full-expansion result.
evidence: The immutable window starts are 0, 72, 110, 182, 254, 326, 398, 470, 542, and 571 with seed 42 and 89 frames per window; start 110 is the frozen accepted anchor.
Dense storyboards reject starts 0, 72, 182, 326, 470, 542, and 571 for visible human face, body, clothing, or a face pop; starts 254 and 398 pass the bounded human-removal review.
Raw candidates are preserved even though the proxy controller returned exit 2, and the experiment manifest records WINDOW_GENERATION_FAILED instead of promoting the batch.
Inspection of Wan preprocessing showed src_face.mp4 contains the source human face and remains an active identity control during replacement generation.
lessons: A clean key window does not imply that the same seed removes the person at different poses; human reappearance must be reviewed per overlap window.
Replacement mode needs an explicit source-face-control policy because a robot reference alone does not prevent the human face crop from being regenerated.
limitations: This batch does not provide a complete human-free full film.
Only human-removal review was completed for the expansion windows; named-flower identity, contact pairing, and strict temporal acceptance are still required.
next_actions: Retake only the failed starts with deterministic source-face-control suppression, preserving the anchor and already acceptable starts.
Run persistent named-flower and hand/contact gates before any overlap stitching.
